text:
New Cocktail & Vinyl Listening Lounge In New York City 🎶🍸💿

If you’re looking for new bars in Brooklyn or a unique NYC date night spot, add Don’t Matter in DUMBO to your list.

📍 55 Sands Street, DUMBO, Brooklyn
🗓️ Wednesday–Sunday
💡 Perfect for: date night, drinks with friends + music lovers

🎶 THE VIBE: Inspired by Japanese listening bars, the space is designed around a curated vinyl collection and custom sound system, with DJs spinning everything from R&B and soul to reggae, hip-hop, rock and more.

🍸 DRINKS: The cocktail menu features some really creative flavor combinations using ingredients like passionfruit, shiso, yuzu, ginger and Thai basil. They also have wine, beer and non-alcoholic options.

🍽️ BITES: Pair your drinks with Pan-Caribbean-inspired small plates made for sharing, including tuna tartlets, shrimp cocktail, crispy mushroom sliders, plantain chips and more.

🌃 THE SPACE: There’s an intimate indoor listening lounge plus an outdoor deck, making it such a cool spot to grab drinks, listen to great music and spend the evening with friends.

Definitely one to put on your radar if you’re looking for new things to do in Brooklyn, cool bars in DUMBO or unique NYC nightlife experiences. 💿✨

SAVE this for your next Brooklyn night out!

text:
@TheLola officially launched a brand-new dinner experience, andI am BLOWN away. From the moment you walk in, you’re met with an elegant, moody cocktail lounge paired with elevated dining energy—chic, warm, and inviting. It’s giving NYC without going to the city 🍸

The LOLA partnered with Chef Brandon “Bud” Carter (current chef at Olea in Spring Lake and former chef at Butcher’s Block) to design a steak, pasta, and seafood-forward menu—and it absolutely delivered. Every dish felt intentional, balanced, and beautifully executed.

What we ordered:
🍸 Dirty Little Secret- dirty martini (extra olive juice, served as two pours)
🍸 Espresso martini
🍸 Bella Ciao 
🍸 French Lace
🥢 Crab rangoon
🐟 Tuna tostada
🍝 Spicy rigatoni
🥩 Ribeye
🍗 Roasted Half Chicken 
🥔 Crispy potatoes

Dessert:
🍩 Churro Crullers 
🍰 Blueberry cheesecake bread pudding 
🍰 Biscoff cheesecake

The cocktail program is elevated with the martini at its core—and it’s absolutely one I’ll be returning for. The bar itself is a vibe on its own: great cocktails, great energy, and perfect for walk-ins.

Good to know:
✨ Elegant dining experience
🕙 Last dinner seating at 10:30 PM
🕑 All rooms open until 2 AM
📅 Reservations release one month in advance—book quickly

We tried the patatas bravas, the onion dip with chips, and the lychee martini, which was honestly one of the best martinis I've had. If you're looking for a new Hoboken restaurant with great food, fun vibes, perfect girls night, and one of the best happy hours in New Jersey, this one deserves a spot on your list.

text:
Big hair. Bigger attitudes. Even bigger memories.
 This wasn’t just a nightclub—it was a rite of passage. A place where nights blurred into dawn, friendships were forged on the dance floor, and the music sealed its legend forever. Joey Harrison’s Surf Club North was wild, woolly, unapologetic, and absolutely unforgettable.

On Saturday, March 14th at 9:30 PM, Franklin Steakhouse becomes the home of that magic once again as Frank Oliver presents Joey Harrison’s Surf Club North Reunion. This is more than a party—it’s a full-blown reunion of an era that defined the 1980s and 1990s Jersey nightlife scene, where chaos ruled and memories were made all year round.

The soundtrack that made Joey’s infamous returns, hosted by the Legendary DJ Jerry DeMeo & DJ Joe D, bringing back the sounds that packed the dance floor and kept the energy raging until sunrise. And for one night, we’re bringing that pure Jersey magic back.

Whether you lived it, survived it, or just heard the stories—this is your chance to reunite with the music, the madness, and the moments that made Joey’s legendary. The memories are calling… and the dance floor is waiting

📍 Visit us at 318 Passaic Ave, Fairfield NJ

text:
Martiny’s

Don’t let the name fool you — this isn’t just a place for a dirty martini. Hidden inside a restored 1800s carriage house in Gramercy, Martiny’s is a three-story Japanese-style cocktail bar led by Takuma Watanabe. The service is meticulous, the cocktails are beautifully executed, and the atmosphere feels impossibly intimate. 🍸✨

The Django

Tucked beneath the Roxy Hotel in TriBeCa, The Django channels the mood of a candlelit Parisian jazz cellar. Think exposed brick, velvet seating, live music, and one of the best late-night atmospheres downtown. 🎷🕯️

Guardian Rooftop

The first rooftop lounge in Union Square and one of NYC’s newest power spots. Located atop the newly redesigned W Hotel, Guardian delivers dramatic skyline views with a sleek, upscale crowd that feels more lounge than nightclub. 🌃🥂

Nubeluz

Perched on the 50th floor of the Ritz-Carlton NoMad, Nubeluz by José Andrés offers some of the most spectacular panoramic views in Manhattan. Chic cocktails, floor-to-ceiling windows, and golden-hour energy make this an easy favorite. ✨🍸

Café Carmellini

Located inside The Fifth Avenue Hotel, this glamorous restaurant by Andrew Carmellini feels like dining inside a European mansion. Towering trees, dramatic interiors, and a crowd that actually dresses for dinner. 🌙🍷

The Portrait Bar

Dark academia meets old New York glamour. Also inside The Fifth Avenue Hotel, The Portrait Bar feels like the private library of a well-traveled aristocrat — moody lighting, velvet seating, and one of the chicest cocktail settings in the city. 🖤📚

text:
This Is One Of The Best Jazz Music & Dinner Experience In New York City 🎺🎶👇🏾

 CLICK THE LINK IN BIO TO BOOK TICKETS 

Django is an underground jazz club combines live music, elevated cocktails, and a full dinner experience inside a candlelit cellar that feels like stepping into old New York. With rotating performances from talented jazz musicians every night, Django offers the perfect mix of live entertainment, romantic ambiance, and classic NYC energy.

🎼Whether you’re searching for the best jazz clubs in NYC, unique date night ideas in Manhattan, or hidden speakeasy-style experiences in Tribeca, Django is a must-visit for anyone wanting to experience the timeless magic of New York City nightlife 🍸

⏳TIME & SCHEDULE
There are two 2 featured performances per evening. Each performance is 2 sets. The first performance set times are 7:30PM-8:30PM and 9PM-10PM. The second performance set times are 10:30PM-11:30PM and 12AM-1AM (On Sundays, all performances are 1 hour earlier with a start time of 6:30PM).

📍WHERE: The Roxy Hotel Cellar, Level 26th Ave, New York 
🎟️COST
Entry to The Django is $35 per person plus a two drink minimum.

text:
📍tomi jazz [midtown east]

finally tried this popular jazz bar! the vibes are immaculate and the curry was like I’ve never had before. if you want to avoid long lines, try to get there before 5pm on a weekday!

what we ordered:
- ⭐️ curry udon 
- 🍜 cod roe udon: SORRY this is really popular but it was tooooo fishy for me :( 
- 🥔 croquette: i think i'm not a fan of croquette’s mushy texture but it wasn’t bad
- 🍸 lemon drop cocktail: delicious but SO strong 

if i could wait early again on a weekday, I’d come back try the omurice! i think this is nice date night spot but it can get quite loud if you’re closer to the band (it comes out at around 5:30pm)

🥂Atmosphere: Known for its romantic and elegant setting, featuring lush floral arrangements and a formal dress code that enhances its “special occasion” appeal.

🍽️ Cuisine: Offers a high-end fixed-price menu with a focus on seasonal ingredients, including signature dishes like the “Brooklyn Bridge” chocolate dessert.

📍 Location: Situated right on the water at 1 Water St, Brooklyn, NY 11201, USA.

🗓️ Schedule: The restaurant is currently open Wednesday through Sunday from 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM (closed Mondays and Tuesdays).

text:
Dinner at cafe zaffri ✨

This place feels less like a restaurant and more like a private club —
marble tables, candlelight, hushed conversations, and that quiet confidence NYC dining does best.

You sit down and immediately slow your pace.
Bread service meant to be shared, cocktails made properly, no rush from course to course.

The menu leans elegant and comforting — pastas with depth, sauces that linger, and a Wellington cooked just right, rich but balanced.
Dessert comes soft and polished, the kind you finish while still talking.

It’s intimate, composed, and discreet.
The kind of room where everyone looks like they belongs there.

Save this for a night you want to feel in the know 🍸🍽️

This is a great spot for date night, plans before a Broadway show, birthday dinner, friends night out, etc. You can also grab a seat at the bar and enjoy their happy hour with $10 and under small bites (no cocktails on the HH).

text:
We ended up at Milk & Roses on a cold night in Greenpoint, the kind of cold that makes you want warmth that lasts longer than the walk inside.

The room held us gently. Low light, warm wood, candle glow softening everything it touched. We ordered Negronis and let the night slow to our pace.

Dinner followed. Pasticcio al Forno and Genovese al ragù di agnello. Both rich, both comforting. The kind of food that settles in, that invites you to stay present.

We sat side by side, hands intertwined, conversation moving easily, drifting and returning. Outside, the backyard garden glowed quietly. Somewhere nearby, a fireplace burned, steady and unhurried.

It was a night to be remembered.
Remembered, and felt.

text:
Looking for great vibes, a fun crowd, and an atmosphere that's always worth the visit? Here are my go-to spots:

1. Temper (NoHo) – Chic cocktails, intimate, perfect for date nights or catching up.

2. Bridges (Chinatown) – Stylish, energetic, and a favorite to start the night.

3. The Lobby Bar at Hotel Chelsea – Timeless, elegant, and ideal for a classic New York cocktail.

4. Othership (Williamsburg) – Lively neighborhood spot with great drinks, music, and an effortlessly cool crowd.

5. The Odeon (Tribeca) – A New York classic with a buzzy dining room that never goes out of style.

6. Tigre (Lower East Side) – Cozy, candlelit, known for creative cocktails and an intimate atmosphere.

7. Raf’s (NoLita) – Beautiful interiors, incredible food, and a lively dinner scene.

8. The Lobby Bar at The Bowery Hotel – One of the city’s coziest hotel bars with a sophisticated crowd.

9. Schmuck (East Village) – Inventive cocktails, fun energy, and one of the coolest bars in the neighborhood.

10. Little Big (Lower East Side) – One of my newest favorites, with creative cocktails, a lively backyard, and a fun atmosphere that's perfect for summer nights.

📍 Save this list for your next night out. Which spot should I check out next? 👇

text:
Some restaurants just get the assignment. These are the dining rooms that work for any group, any mood, and any reason to get together.

Nubiani NYC, with locations in Midtown and Koreatown, is ideal for groups. It serves standout Korean BBQ in a sleek, modern space made for sharing banchan, perfectly cooked short ribs, and signature dishes, all guided by an attentive team that keeps the table flowing.

In Greenpoint, Oxomoco is a go-to for shareable plates. Wood fired Mexican cooking meets candlelit warmth in a space that feels intimate while still buzzing with energy.

Le Bar Penelope on the Upper East Side is perfect for girls’ night. Parisian charm, shareable plates, and cocktails that keep the conversation going make it easy to linger longer than planned.

At Lincoln Center, Tatiana by Chef Kwame is ideal before a Broadway show. Steps from the theaters, it brings bold Afro Caribbean flavors like braised oxtails and piri piri salad in a fun, purple lit space that sets the tone for the night.

And Freemans Restaurant remains a classic for brunch or a hearty dinner. A cozy farmhouse setting pairs perfectly with comfort driven plates, from apple cinnamon french toast to Amish chicken and pork chops.

text:
Every New Yorker knows the place to catch up and have a great night with friends isn’t a cramped apartment — here are my favorite spots around the city right now that are perfect for group dinners.

1. Lil’ Frankie’s
My take: the cutest italian spot in the ev, perfect for dinner with friends or family. it has an authentically italian, old-school speakeasy vibe that gets more fun as the night goes on — just remember it’s cash only.
My standouts: roasted eggplant, any pizza

2. Rosie’s
My take: my classic go-to mexican spot for birthdays or celebrations. reservations are easy to get, prices are fair, and the drinks are strong (in the best way).
My standouts: guacamole, quesabirria, assorted tacos, piña marg, coco loco marg

3. Zou Zou’s
My take: one of my favorite mediterranean spots in the city. great atmosphere without feeling stuffy in hudson yards, with shareable dishes, solid service, and fair pricing for nyc.
My standouts: dip platter, latkes, filet skewer, artichoke, jeweled rice, kasseri cheese

4. Port Sa’id
My take: a mediterranean-israeli inspired spot that’s perfect for group celebrations. cool, trendy vibe and the west village location makes it ideal for a pre-going-out dinner.
My standouts: tahini, hummus, leafy salad, lamb kebob

5. Flame
My take: a quintessential hibachi spot for birthdays or special occasions with shockingly good service and food. prices are extremely reasonable for how much you get, and the hibachi tables seat around nine people.
My standouts: steak and shrimp combo

6. Chi
My take: one of my favorite slept-on asian-inspired spots in the city. reservations aren’t too hard to get, groups are always welcomed, and the food and service are consistently great — especially for nyc pricing.
My standouts: cucumber salad, spare ribs, pan-fried pork dumplings, wontons in chili oil, scallion pancake

7. Street Taco
My take: an easy go-to mexican spot for tacos, margs, and good vibes before a night out. the kips bay / gramercy location makes it super convenient to east village bars, and it’s probably the most budget-friendly spot on this list.
My standouts: guacamole, yuca fries, any taco, pineapple marg, watermelon marg

8. Little Ways
My take: a very cute two-story townhouse-style spot that’s perfect for groups or special occasions. the booth areas are ideal for larger parties — definitely request one when booking.
My standouts: mussels, cheeseburger, deviled eggs

9. Blue Ribbon (Sullivan St.)
My take: my go-to group sushi spot with a chill vibe and consistently great sushi. perfect for a casual night catching up with friends.
My standouts: crispy rice, popcorn shrimp, negi hama

10. La Pecora Bianca
My take: a true nyc staple for good reason. always consistent, multiple locations across the city, and rarely hard to get a reservation — my fallback when i don’t want the stress of a weekend reservation hunt.
My standouts: rigatoni vodka, crispy artichoke, whipped ricotta, crispy brussels sprouts, truffle tagliatelle

text:
In a borough known for bold flavors and late-night food culture, @Pookie Bakery is quickly becoming one of Brooklyn’s sweetest success stories.

Tucked inside a longtime neighborhood café on Coney Island Avenue, the cookie shop has built a loyal following with oversized gourmet cookies, molten cookie tins, house made soft-serve, and a family-centered story rooted in community.

The bakery was founded by Muheed Ali, a Brooklyn entrepreneur who first started baking cookies at home for friends and relatives before he was encouraged to offer them at the Gyro Café 🙏 Customers immediately responded, returning for more and spreading the word throughout the neighborhood.

What began as a side project soon transformed into its own brand 🍪 Today, Pookie Bakery has become known for its signature “Big Body Cookies” — thick, six-ounce creations baked with rich butter, premium chocolate, crisp edges, and soft gooey centers.

Among the bakery’s standout flavors are the classic Chocolate Chip Cookie, loaded with Belgian chocolate and baked until perfectly soft in the center 🤤 Other customer favorites include the Nutella Stuffed Cookie, Oreo Cookie, Reese’s Peanut Butter Cup Cookie, White Chocolate Lava Cookie, and the increasingly popular Dubai Chocolate Lava Cookie.

But the true star of the menu may be Pookie’s Signature Cookie Tin Collection. Served warm in its own baking tin and paired with scoops of ice cream, the dessert has become a social media-worthy indulgence designed for sharing. The cookie tin features caramelized edges with a molten center that slowly melts together with the ice cream for an over-the-top dessert experience.

#pookiebakery #coneyislandave #brooklyn #brooklynnyc

text:
Every woman deserves to feel dignified — no matter her circumstances. That belief is at the heart of why the 𝗡𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝗝𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲𝘆 𝗖𝗹𝘂𝗯 has proudly supported 𝗜 𝗦𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗚𝗶𝗿𝗹𝘀 for 𝘀𝗶𝘅 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 — and they are not stopping now. 💪🏾

This year, under the dedicated leadership of 𝗡𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝗝𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲𝘆 𝗖𝗹𝘂𝗯 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘇𝗻𝗲𝗿, the Club collected and donated:

🩱 𝟰𝟱 𝗻𝗲𝘄 & 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝗿𝗮𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝘃𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝘇𝗲𝘀 & 𝗰𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗿𝘀
🏃🏾‍♀️ 𝟭𝟬 𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘀 𝗯𝗿𝗮𝘀

These donations were delivered to the 𝗜 𝗦𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗚𝗶𝗿𝗹𝘀 drop-off location in 𝗦𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗳𝗶𝗲𝗹𝗱, 𝗡𝗝 and will go directly to women and girls experiencing homelessness, domestic violence, poverty, and distress — because dignity should never be out of reach.

𝗜 𝗦𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗚𝗶𝗿𝗹𝘀 is a global nonprofit movement that collects bras, underwear, and menstrual hygiene products and gets them safely into the hands of those who need them most. Their mission is simple and powerful: 𝗠𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗗𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗼𝗿𝗺. 🌍💜

Thank you, 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘇𝗻𝗲𝗿, for championing this effort year after year on behalf of the North Jersey Club. And thank you to every Club member who contributed — your generosity is changing lives one donation at a time. 🙏🏾 We are proud to call you part of the 𝗛𝗚 𝗠𝗰𝗖𝘂𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗨𝗽𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝟭𝟮 family!

To learn more or donate, visit 🌐 𝘄𝘄𝘄.𝗶𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗿𝗹𝘀.𝗼𝗿𝗴

This spot was a highlight for us during NYCWFF, where we were surrounded by some of the most celebrated chefs in the industry, including Geoffrey Zakarian and Michael Voltaggio.

Perfect for: elevated date nights, after-work cocktails, or a classy night downtown.

text:
215 Chrystie St, New York, NY 10002 

I had a blast at The Roof at PUBLIC Hotel’s indoor lounge in Manhattan. The glass-enclosed space offered unreal NYC skyline views, with a chic vibe and solid DJ tunes. I sipped a $18 Frosé St. Tropez (cocktails $15-$20, beers $8-$10, wines $12-$15), munched on $10-$20 small plates like sliders, and soaked in the upscale atmosphere. Happy hour (5-7 PM, Mon-Fri) saved me a few bucks. Dropped about $45 per person with tip—pricey but worth it for the views and vibe. Dress sharp and book ahead; it’s a hot spot!

#TheNewYorkPlace #NYCRooftops #ManhattanVibes #TheRoofPUBLIC #NYCNightlife

text:
Hi guys 👋🏼 

I’ve finally gotten myself together and decided to start sharing my favorite NYC spots with you 🙌🏼
I definitely haven’t been everywhere because that’s simply impossible 🥹

 Did you know there are over 17,600 restaurants in New York City , not counting the thousands of bars, cafés, food trucks, and pop-ups?
It would take years—decades even! 
But! I’m on a mission to discover something new and interesting—and share it with you, little by little 🤏🏼

So here’s how I’m kicking things off: 
jazz clubs 🎺

I’m a huge jazz lover, and I’ve made a personal project of visiting as many as I can. 
Here’s my current top list—each one is cozy, beautifully atmospheric, and features amazing musicians 🍷 

My Top Jazz Clubs in NYC 
all cozy, beautiful, and full of musical magic 🪄 
	•	Zinc Bar    
	•	Django 
	•	The Nines
	•	Bemelmans 
	•	Blue Note
	•	Melody’s 
	•	Ornithology
	•	Vanguard
	•	Smalls 
	•	Joe’s Pub
	•	Somewhere Nowhere
	•	Soho Grand 
	•	Aman 
	•	St. Tuesday
	•	Arora

(I’ll keep updating this list with more locations as I go—NYC is full of hidden gems, after all.)

🫵🏻 Your turn! 
What are your favorite jazz or live-music spots? Drop your go-to places in the comments so we can keep the recommendations rolling.

text:
Some of the biggest names in music history all played some of their first sets on the same NYC stage.

@The Bitter End opened in 1961 and is the oldest rock and roll club in all of NYC. Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell, Stevie Wonder, James Taylor, and Lady Gaga have all graced this same stage on their way to becoming legends. I came to see @kingsland perform, a NYC based pop soul band with eight members and a fantastic sound. Every piece of the bands adds a layer of rhythm that works together to create a genuinely unique experience.

If you love live music in NYC, check out the legendary Bitter End and follow Kingsland for updates on their next concert!

If you want to see more unique and unforgettable New York experiences, follow along as I continue to explore the city.

📍The Bitter End
147 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10012

One of the hottest spots in the city right now for a reason. Maison Close nails the dinner-to-party transition, with a high-energy crowd and a vibe that feels both exclusive and electric.

• Faena Living Room 🎶
For a more elevated birthday, this space blends live performances and DJ sets without ever feeling like a full-on club. It’s sophisticated, stylish, and ideal for a more refined celebration.

• The Blond 🪩
A go-to for fun, nostalgic music—think 2000s and 2010s hits everyone knows. The space is larger than most downtown lounges, making it perfect for big birthday groups.

• Jean’s (Downstairs) 🔊
Hidden beneath the popular restaurant, this underground spot leans into house, techno, and crowd-favorite tracks. If your birthday vibe is more music-driven and high-energy, this is the move.

text:
If you’re looking for an upscale dinner experience in New York City, Cathedral is one you should add to your list.

I came here for a solo birthday dinner, and from the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was exactly what I was looking for. Dark, elegant, intimate, and perfect for a date night, birthday dinner, or just treating yourself.

The dinner rolls might honestly be some of the best I’ve ever had. I had to order them twice. For my entrée, I went with the prime ribeye and fries, and the steak was cooked perfectly and packed with flavor.

And I have to mention the restroom because NYC restaurants have a secret competition going on. It was spotless, beautifully designed, and smelled like I walked straight into the perfume section at Macy’s.

My total came to about $120 before tip, which I didn’t think was bad at all for an upscale solo birthday dinner in NYC.

text:
1. Maison Close
Maison Close is the perfect pick if you want something sexy, upscale, and a little exclusive. It’s ideal for a group that wants dinner and a party in one place—think dim lighting, great energy, and a seamless transition into dancing.

2. Faena Living Room
For a more elevated night, Faena Living Room brings the full experience. Live performances early on turn into a DJ-led party later, making it feel polished, glamorous, and anything but basic.

3. The Blond
The Blond is always a crowd-pleaser for groups. It’s spacious, easy to navigate with a big party, and the music (think 2000s–2010s hits) keeps everyone dancing all night.

4. Club Room at Soho Grand
A go-to for groups in their late 20s and early 30s. The vibe is fun but still polished, with throwback hits and a crowd that knows how to party without it feeling chaotic.

5. La Victoria
If your group wants a Latin party vibe, La Victoria delivers. Expect high energy, great music, and a dance floor that stays packed all night—perfect for a lively, unforgettable celebration.

text:
• The Nines — A chic piano lounge with light bites, candlelight, and classic old-NYC energy. Always check Resy or IG for Thanksgiving-week hours before planning dinner.

• The Django — Subterranean jazz at The Roxy with vaulted brick ceilings, cocktails, dinner, and nightly live music. A warm, moody escape from the cold.

• Portrait Bar — A glamorous Fifth Avenue hideaway with rich wood paneling, a carved stone fireplace, museum-level art, and refined cocktails by Darryl Chan.

• Nubeluz — A glittering José Andrés rooftop above the Ritz-Carlton NoMad. Panoramic skyline views, sleek design, and modern classic cocktails for winter nights.

• Titsou Bar — A Paris-inspired speakeasy tucked inside Fouquet’s Tribeca. Plush, intimate, and perfect for cozy cocktails behind a hidden door.

• Baccarat Bar — A jewel-box lounge inside the Baccarat Hotel serving Champagne and cocktails in sparkling crystal. Pure winter glamour.

.

.
.
.

#WinterInNYC #NYCBars #WinterVibesNYC #NYCNightlife #CozyNYC

text:
Lost in the magic of a New York night ✨
Sitting in one of Manhattan’s hidden luxury restaurants, surrounded by candlelight, soft jazz, and the sound of glasses clinking in the background. The city outside never sleeps, but inside this moment, time feels slower. Dressed in black, enjoying an unforgettable dinner with fine wine, elegant conversation, and the energy only New York can give.
There’s something about NYC at night — the lights reflecting through the windows, the atmosphere filled with ambition, romance, and mystery. Every table has a story, every street outside carries a dream, and every moment feels like a scene from a movie. From the warm glow of the restaurant to the late-night skyline waiting outside, this is the kind of evening you never want to end.
Luxury isn’t always about money… sometimes it’s about the feeling. The confidence, the calm, the vibe, the people around you, and the memories being created in silence between conversations. New York teaches you to enjoy the moment, appreciate the energy, and live like the night belongs to you.
A perfect dinner, a beautiful atmosphere, and the city of dreams all in one frame. 🖤🍷🌃

Rampoldi brings the glamour of Monte-Carlo to the Upper West Side with a menu that beautifully blends French and Italian flavors.

🍸Caesar Salad

🍸Red Wine Braised Beef 
🍸Lobster Pasta

Valentine’s Day is coming up and it’s time to get booking a romantic dinner spot for you and your significant other (or bestie, obviously) 🫶🏼

These are my favourite and most romantic restaurants in New York that are perfect for Valentine’s Day 💘

The full list over on the blog has 19 restaurants across Manhattan and Brooklyn 🗽

but the ones I’ve featured are my top top favourites and restaurants I keep going back to time and time again 😮‍💨

🍝 Malatesta Trattoria: for the best Italian

🥂 Butter: if it’s good enough for Blair Waldorf…

🇫🇷 Le French Diner: incredibly intimate and dark (but you might have to wait a while for a seat)

🥩 Keens Steakhouse: it doesn’t get much more classic New York than this

🎷 Ammazzacaffe: dark intimate lighting, incredible food and live jazz music - the perfect date spot

🧆 Cafe Mogador: if you’d like to add a little Middle Eastern flavour to your Valentine’s

🍣 Sushi Kai: an intimate 16 course omakase? Yes please

As I mentioned, there are many more choices in the full blog post, but I highly recommend the list above too 🫶🏼

What are your Valentine’s Day plans? 💘

text:
❗️INSANE UNDERGROUND RESTAURANT IN NYC: DO NOT DISTURB 🔥 This hidden gem is tucked underneath the streets of Manhattan’s West Village and waiting inside is a crazy menu of food + all types of vibes. Do Not Disturb has become one of my favorite city joints and it’s not hard to see why. 

📌 In terms of food, you can dig into both humble grub as well as curated high end plates. All are chef crafted and crush it on unique but wildly delicious flavor. The crispy rice selection is top tier, the Smashburger is easily one of Manhattans best & their lemon pepper wings BANG. But if you want something a bit more fancy, the lobster pasta is a sure shot and the lamb is *chefs kiss* 

👉 But what makes this place even more of a standout is the various vibes you’ll find throughout there multiple rooms. You can easily have a beautiful date night here or hit it for a friend’s night out and honestly it will deliver equally on both moods. 

🫡 Throw this West Village hidden gem at the top of your NYC grub list & thank me later. 

📍 West Village, Manhattan, NYC

text:
Vinyl Steakhouse is a music-driven dining concept that blends a classic steakhouse experience with the soul of a vintage record shop, creating one of the most unique dinners in New York City. 🎵📀

What sets Vinyl Steakhouse apart is its curated vinyl collection with thousands of records line the walls, and guests can often select or influence the music playing during their meal. 

It’s like dining inside a high-end listening lounge rather than a traditional steakhouse.

🥩On the culinary side, Vinyl Steakhouse focuses on elevated steakhouse fare with a modern edge. Expect expertly cooked premium cuts, refined sides, and thoughtful plating that balances indulgence with polish. The menu is designed to feel familiar yet elevated, appealing to both classic steakhouse lovers and a younger, design-forward crowd.

🥃The atmosphere is a major draw:
* Vintage-inspired interiors
* Warm lighting and moody tones
* A laid-back but upscale energy
* Music that becomes part of the experience, not background noise

It’s the kind of place that works equally well for a date night, celebration dinner in nyc, group dinner, especially for guests who care as much about ambiance as they do about food.

📍WHERE: Vinyl Steakhouse
35W 19th St New York, NY

text:
✨ If you’re looking for the most unforgettable NYC places to eat, Cecconi’s in DUMBO should be at the top of your list. Sitting outside with views of the Brooklyn Bridge and Manhattan skyline, you get the perfect mix of incredible food and iconic New York vibes. 🍕🥂

From wood-fired pizza and spritz cocktails to romantic candlelit tables right by the water, this spot defines the magic of dining out in the city. Whether you’re planning date night, catching up with friends, or just searching for new places to go out and eat with a view, Cecconi’s delivers every time. 🌉🌆

NYC is filled with amazing restaurants, but few combine delicious Italian food with this kind of sunset backdrop. If you’re exploring DUMBO or Brooklyn Bridge Park, make sure to stop by it’s a dining experience that feels both elevated and cozy. 🗽✨ #nyc #nycskyline #dumbo #nycfood #nycviews

text:
Why just have dinner when you can have dinner and a party? These spots start with great food and end with music, dancing, and unforgettable energy:

1️⃣ Maison Close (SoHo) – French “vibe dining” where the lights dim, shows start, and dinner turns into a nightclub.
2️⃣ Crazy Pizza (SoHo) – Pizza disco ball, dough-tossing, napkin-waving, and thin-crust magic.
3️⃣ Little Prince (SoHo) – A Parisian-style bistro with steak frites, a famous onion soup burger, and lively charm.
4️⃣ Kyma (Flatiron) – Mykonos vibes, DJs, dancing between courses, and opa-worthy brunches.
5️⃣ HaSalon (Midtown) – Tel Aviv energy, late-night seatings, and dancing on chairs with shareable feasts.

✨ Bottom line: NYC has mastered the art of dinner that turns into a dance floor. Where are you booking first?

Forget the hyped spots, these late-night joints are where you really want to eat. Real food, no frills, and open late. Hit these places when the tourists are asleep:

• El Castillo de Jagua – Dominican diner, no BS, just good chicken.
• Pata Paplean – Thai street food in a dive bar, perfect for night owls.
• Ba Xuyên – Some of the best banh mi in the city, and cheap.
• Fat Buddha – Asian fusion, booze, and killer wings.
• Casa Adela – Puerto Rican rotisserie that’ll hit the spot.
• El Atoradero – Mexican food that’s actually legit.
• Benemon – Quiet Japanese comfort food, because ramen’s better at night.

Eat, don’t post.

text: Afterhours Clubs in NYC (2026): Do They Still Exist? The Rise, Fall & Secret After Parties. New York City has always been known as “the city that never sleeps,” but when it comes to afterhours clubs in 2026, the scene looks very different from what it used to be. The Rise of Afterhours Culture Back in the golden era of nightlife, afterhours clubs were a core part of NYC’s party culture. Legendary venues like The Loft and Paradise Garage helped shape the idea that the party didn’t end at 4 a.m. — it simply moved to the next location. From disco to underground house and techno, afterhours spots became safe spaces for music lovers, creatives, and night owls who wanted more than the typical club night. The Fall of Traditional Afterhours Clubs Fast forward to 2026, and true afterhours clubs are rare in NYC. Why? * Strict 4 a.m. closing laws * High rent and operating costs * Increased regulations on nightlife venues * Many iconic nightlife spaces either closed, rebranded, or shifted into event-based formats instead of running full-time afterhours operations. The New Era: Secret After Parties While official afterhours clubs may be fading, the culture itself is far from dead. It has simply gone underground. Today’s afterhours scene lives through: * Invite-only warehouse parties * Private loft events * Pop-up sunrise sessions * Word-of-mouth RSVP gatherings Neighborhoods like Brooklyn — especially areas around creative hubs — are now the heartbeat of these hidden parties, where DJs play until sunrise and sometimes beyond. Clubs That Stretch the Night (But Not Officially “Afterhours”) Some modern venues still host extended sets and marathon events, especially electronic music spaces like Elsewhere and House of Yes, but they operate within legal time limits and event structures. So, Do Afterhours Clubs Still Exist in 2026? Go to www.kingofnyc.net/blog for details. #NYC NYCNightlife #NewYorkCity

text:
🌙✨ Late-night drinks at Barbam @barbamnyc (Ktown NYC) ✨🌙

This Korean-inspired cocktail bar has some of the most beautiful presentations I’ve seen—and the flavors are just as good. Perfect vibe for hanging out late into the night 🍸💫

We ordered:
🍷 JMT — super romantic, lit with little “stars” ✨ whiskey-based but not too heavy, more on the citrusy sweet side.
🍓 Hulu Punch — adorable look, sweet & creamy with a strawberry ice-candy vibe.
🥃 Naengmyeon — refreshing whiskey (Whiskey + Cucumber + Maemil)
🫧 Oedo Botania — light, bubbly, and so pretty; great if you want something refreshing and easy to drink.

Every cocktail felt like a little story blending Korean culture & creativity. Perfect spot for late-night drinks & hangouts in Ktown 🌙 Definitely coming back!

text:
Where to Dance to 2010s Throwbacks in New York

1. Acme
  A reliable late-night spot if you want dancing without the full club pressure. Easy entry, fun crowd, and the kind of music that keeps people moving.
2. The Blond
  A polished hotel lounge that turns into a packed dance room later at night. Expect 2010s hits, throwbacks, and a crowd that actually comes to dance.
3. Faena Living Room
  Starts refined with cocktails and piano-bar energy, then slowly turns into a lively supper-club style night with music and a more mature crowd.
4. Paul’s Baby Grand
  A small, high-energy SoHo/Tribeca club with a fun crowd and big throwback energy. Arrive early because it fills up fast.

The Seaview Diner, once located at 2136 Rockaway Parkway in Canarsie, Brooklyn, was a beloved neighborhood staple. Known for its late-night vibes and proximity to the Bayview Houses and Belt Parkway, it became a go-to spot for locals to gather, eat, and connect. Sadly, the diner was demolished before 2009 and replaced by an apartment building, but it remains a cherished part of Canarsie's history.

text:
Do you remember Charles Pizzeria in Sunset Park?
For 57 years, Charles Pizzeria at 4910 Fifth Avenue served up some of the best slices in Brooklyn. From after-school hangouts to late-night cravings, it was more than just a pizzeria—it was part of the neighborhood’s heart. Generations of Sunset Park families grew up with those red booths, handwritten menus, and the unmistakable smell of a fresh pie coming out of the oven. Though the ovens went cold in 2021, the memories are still hot.

text:
New York City’s rooftop bars are more than just glamorous hangouts — they’re a living part of the city’s cultural evolution, blending architecture, nightlife, and skyline romance into one unforgettable experience.

The roots of rooftop socializing in New York trace back to the early 1900s, during the Golden Age of Broadway. As summer heat made enclosed theaters unbearable, hotel owners began opening rooftop gardens and open-air cafés atop grand hotels. Venues like the Astor Roof Garden (opened in 1904) and the Hotel Knickerbocker’s rooftop ballroom became fashionable escapes where the city’s elite could dine under the stars while listening to live orchestras. These spaces set the foundation for what would later become today’s modern rooftop bar culture — luxury and leisure elevated, quite literally, above the city bustle.

After a mid-century lull, rooftop nightlife re-emerged in the 1980s and 1990s, as Manhattan’s skyline became an icon of urban sophistication. Trendy venues like the Rainbow Room at Rockefeller Center revived the allure of panoramic views paired with cocktails, while the rise of boutique hotels brought an entirely new wave of elevated experiences.

We didn’t just throw parties. We changed nightlife in our city.
That same energy never left me. I just found a new arena.

And today I found the plug.
Not a person. A literal plug.

And what I do with it this Sunday at this open house in Passaic Park is going to hit different.

Drop a 🎉 if you remember Club Rain or Tropicanas.
